outcome: A single petabyte-scale archive namespace where capacity grows without a migration and cold content still stays reachable at the same path.
overview: Media archives grow in a way that defeats conventional storage planning: content is never deleted, resolution keeps rising, and the same asset is needed at unpredictable moments years after it was made. PowerScale scales out as one namespace so capacity grows without a migration, and tiering moves cold content to cheaper media while keeping it reachable at the same path. The design question that decides cost is how much content is genuinely cold, and that can only be answered by profiling access rather than by taking an age threshold for granted.

benefits.text: Capacity grows within one namespace, so growth does not mean a migration project
benefits.limits: Sized from measured capacity and performance data; a design built on invoice history or on projected growth alone produces a quotation rather than an architecture

benefits.text: Cold content moves to cheaper media while staying reachable at the same path
benefits.limits: Tiering economics depend on how much content is genuinely cold, which must be profiled; an age-based assumption routinely overstates it

benefits.text: Production workflows reach the archive over standard file protocols without integration work
benefits.limits: Protocol compatibility is not performance; a workflow that assumed local storage may still need its access pattern reviewed

residency: Content remains on customer-owned equipment; broadcast archives stay in-country where regulation requires it

notFor.why: Scale-out file storage serves unstructured content; databases have different access and latency requirements

notFor.situation: An archive that is genuinely write-once and never read
notFor.why: Object or tape economics are materially better where retrieval is rare and latency-tolerant

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Dell implementation partner · Duration: 10–14 weeks to a consolidated archive, hardware lead time excluded
Support model: Vendor hardware support with a replacement term matched to production criticality; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed capacity and tiering review.
1) Assessment — capacity, growth projection, access profiling and facility headroom
2) Design — tier split, tiering policy, namespace layout and consolidation plan
3) Deploy — nodes installed, namespace established, protocols presented
4) Consolidate and hand over — archive consolidated, tiering active, operations handed over
